summary: Listed in a 2016 Georgia lookout index in Jones County with a GFC number; no source found gives its build, staffing or fate.

evidence.supports: Index row: lookout listed in Jones County, with notes 'griswoldville' and 'gfc-607'
Index column heading names the last column as the GFC number
evidence.quote: GA tower list lat/lon, elevation, GFC number

evidence.supports: Index map was last revised in March 2016
Griswoldville was an industrial village in Jones County on the Central of Georgia Railway
evidence.quote: Griswoldville, an industrial village on the Central of Georgia Railway in Jones County

evidence.supports: The village produced cotton gins before the war and Confederate revolvers during it
evidence.quote: produced cotton gins during the antebellum period and Confederate revolvers during the Civil War (1861-65)

evidence.supports: Union forces under Sherman destroyed the village on his march to the sea
evidence.quote: The village was destroyed during Union general William T. Sherman’s march to the sea

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The only source naming this tower is the tnlandforms Georgia lookout index (row GA219). A WebSearch on the name and Griswoldville found no tower history, and the NHLR Georgia index in the local cache does not list it. The Griswoldville link for the note 'griswoldville' is unconfirmed and the story says so. The brief's GFC US 607 matches the index's gfc-607 and needs no correction. Before publishing a status, check with the Georgia Forestry Commission or the Jones County historical society. Story is short by necessity.
